label: copy phase: fed-back f input late in the copy, strongest when the token after f is 2
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, never in the original phase or on <DEL>. About 95% of activation mass is on steps where the fed-back input is f, i.e. the model just output f and is now outputting the token that followed f. It never fires on the first occurrence of a token, so it only sees f that was already seen in the original. It is mostly at recall_idx >= 3 (rare at recall 2, none at 0-1) and near the end of the sequence (to_go 0-2). Magnitude depends strongly on the token being output now: every top activation (about 0.9-1.0 of max) is f followed by 2, and out_tok=2 carries 37% of the mass. p, r, o and 3 come next, then z, h, c, k, f and l. The bare rule (copy phase, input f) gets 92% recall but only 11% precision. Most f inputs whose next token is something else (j, y, 0, n, t, ...) stay inactive. Restricting the output token to that set raises F1 to about 0.5, so the token list is partly fitted. A small leftover of weak activations sits on inputs 2, p and r (a few percent of mass).

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=f (+7.62), phase=2 & in_tok=2 (+6.04), phase=2 & in_tok=p (+4.57), phase=2 & in_tok=r (+3.88), prev_tok=s (+3.70), in_tok=f (+3.61). Lower it: correct=1 (-5.67), recall_idx=1 (-3.95), prev_tok=<DEL> (-3.95), out_tok=v (-3.49).
